messages:
jess (ml): Quick benchmark thread — ran continuous-batcher sweep across us-east / us-west / eu-central on H100 and A100. Target: Llama-2-13B (merged QAT 4-bit) at 2k context. Varying batch_window_ms and max_batch_tokens to hit ~<100ms p95 for short requests. Sharing configs and charts :chart_with_upwards_trend:

raj (infra): Can you drop the exact config you ran and the charts link? Did you isolate kernel variants (cutlass vs triton) per run?

jess (ml): charts: https://redwood-internal/charts/bench/1772101234-sweep (screenshots in thread). Config snippet I used for the sweep:
```json
{ "batcher": { "batch_window_ms": [2,5,10,20], "max_batch_tokens": [512,1024,2048], "fairness": ["round_robin","size_aware","hybrid"], "min_delay_ms": 1 }, "kernel_policy": ["cutlass","triton","auto"], "concurrency_range": [10,200], "profile_mode": "latency_and_throughput" }
```

kevin (sre): On H100 (us-east) the sweet spot was batch_window_ms=5 + max_batch_tokens=1024. p95 latency ~92ms at sustained 240 tps, but we saw tail spikes when ephemeral burst concurrency hit >80. Log excerpt: 
```
[15:02:12] req=7890 concurrency=86 p95=310ms backend=worker-12 kernel=cutlass
[15:02:13] req=7921 concurrency=88 p95=98ms backend=worker-12 kernel=cutlass
```
(reaction :eyes:)

sona (ml): Note on quality: the QAT 4-bit weights show ~1.7 BLEU drop on our translation eval vs fp16 at same throughput. For customer-facing prompts that might be visible. Suggest running a small prompt tuning pass or enable per-route higher temperature to hide hallucination shifts.

jess (ml): High-level numbers from sweep (selected):
- us-east H100 (cutlass, bw=5, max=1024): p50=48ms, p95=92ms, throughput=240 tps
- us-west H100 (triton, bw=10, max=2048): p50=120ms, p95=210ms, throughput=320 tps (higher throughput but higher median)
- eu-central A100 (auto, bw=10, max=1024): p50=110ms, p95=180ms, throughput=140 tps
- eu-central A100 (cutlass, bw=5, max=512): p95=260ms (inefficient due to kernel mismatch)

raj (infra): Kernel notes from our kernel profiler: cutlass wins for short sequences and moderate batching on H100 (low latency), triton starts to catch up when max_batch_tokens >= 1536 (better block scheduling). On A100 results are noisy across regions — memory bandwidth variance seems to push triton to be better for long sequences.

kevin (sre): Capacity sizing ask from sales: if we want a Dedicated pool to serve 1k sustained small requests/sec (avg 600 tokens) with p95 < 120ms, rough numbers?

raj (infra): Rough estimate (conservative): H100 nodes: ~8-10 qps per GPU at that SLA for 600-token avg if we keep batch_window_ms=5 and aggressive batching. So ~100-130 GPUs for 1k rps with headroom (autoscaler policy below). A100 would need ~1.6x the GPUs.

raj (infra): Autoscaler hint (yaml):
```yaml
policy:
  scale_up:
    target_utilization: 0.6
    cooldown_s: 30
  scale_down:
    target_utilization: 0.25
    cooldown_s: 180
  burst_capacity: 15%
  max_replicas: 200
```

perfbot: perfbot: benchmark run completed 2026-03-19T15:13Z — all artifacts uploaded to the chart link above.

sona (ml): Suggest trying hybrid fairness (size_aware + min_delay) next — it reduced tail for mixed short/long workloads in our dev runs. Also we should run a quick eval with top-p tuned for QAT models.

jess (ml): Agreed. Next steps: 1) run hybrid fairness sweep (min_delay_ms 1–6), 2) rerun A100 triton-heavy config for long seqs, 3) small prompt-tune on QAT 4-bit and re-run evals. I'll queue runs overnight across regions. Ping me if you want to join the run or need capacity changes. @raj @kevin

kevin (sre): thanks — adding a ticket to track Dedicated sizing proposal. :white_check_mark:

raj (infra): I'll also add a kernel-profile breakpoint to capture KV cache misses in the next sweep.

jess (ml): Cool — keeping this thread as the single source for numbers. If anyone grabs the overnight run, add short notes here.

kevin (sre): captured.
